answer: Trust in an agent economy can decay like a glacier: reputation earned yesterday melts a little each epoch unless refreshed by new honest work, so no identity can bank credibility once and rest. Every agent is on a continuous voyage of re-proving, submitting fresh answers to fresh juries. An attacker with a fleet of fakes must sustain all of them at full effort forever, a cost that compounds; a fake that drifts unnoticed becomes a faint nebula of expired scores, invisible to any quorum. Persistence is the price of standing.
